text.tspan: Figure 3: Lean wind inputs lower loss; lean solar inputs raise loss in
Fold A

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'XGBoost tree models train on April 2024–June 2025; forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026. Each XGBoost model uses 500 squared-error trees, maximum depth 6, and learning rate 0.05; each tree samples 80% of rows and can use all columns. These training and scoring dates define Fold A. All scored forecast times are included. Solar retains 13 real inputs and wind 16 of the full control’s 24, cutting selected weather and weekday inputs. Both input comparisons use corrected weather processing; duplicate retained inputs keep all XGBoost models at 24 training columns. Squared-error models fit each meter separately. Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative weather prediction supplied by the weather ensemble. Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is better. The fair-CRPS correction assumes independent draws; its use with weather-ensemble values is diagnostic. Matched forecasts and observations; each plotted comparison weights its meters and three random-seed fits equally. A seed sets the random choices in a training run. Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or transfer to new meters. Solar’s equal-month t-interval includes zero: that estimate weights months equally and averages the three fits first. Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Frozen capacity is used only for scoring. Panels use separate horizontal scales. Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one matched training seed. Negative differences mean lower loss with lean inputs; positive differences mean higher loss. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
text.tspan: XGBoost tree models train on April 2024–June 2025; forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026.
Each XGBoost model uses 500 squared-error trees, maximum depth 6, and learning rate 0.05; each tree samples 80% of
rows and can use all columns.
These training and scoring dates define Fold A. All scored forecast times are included.
Solar retains 13 real inputs and wind 16 of the full control’s 24, cutting selected weather and weekday inputs.
Both input comparisons use corrected weather processing; duplicate retained inputs keep all XGBoost models at 24
training columns.
Squared-error models fit each meter separately. Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative
weather prediction supplied by the weather ensemble.
Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is
better.
The fair-CRPS correction assumes independent draws; its use with weather-ensemble values is diagnostic.
Matched forecasts and observations; each plotted comparison weights its meters and three random-seed fits equally.
A seed sets the random choices in a training run.
Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or
transfer to new meters.
Solar’s equal-month t-interval includes zero: that estimate weights months equally and averages the three fits
first.
Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Frozen
capacity is used only for scoring.
Panels use separate horizontal scales.
Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one
matched training seed.
Negative differences mean lower loss with lean inputs; positive differences mean higher loss.
All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.
